# Utilities {#utilities}

Tools that help with DWARPH, in your browser. Nothing you type in them is sent anywhere.

## Schedule builder {#schedule-builder}

This page is a tool, not a description of one. Fill in the form and it writes the schedule file (`schedule.json`) for you, checking as you go for the mistakes that cost people an experiment --- a temperature the hardware will refuse, a light level outside the allowed range, two setpoints at the same time, a setpoint the cycle never reaches.

A schedule is only the experiment: temperature and light over time, the picture interval and how long the run lasts. The device's own set-up --- its Wi-Fi network, its focus and its light calibration --- is in its other file, `config.json`, which the device writes itself ([Settings on the SD card](device.html#sd-files)); there is no builder for it. So the same schedule can run on any number of devices, and it holds no passwords.

Everything happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Start from one of the four presets and change the numbers, or build a cycle from scratch. The graph shows what the chamber will actually do, which is usually enough to catch a schedule that does not mean what you thought it meant.

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Emit the tool as a raw HTML block so pandoc passes it through verbatim
# rather than parsing the markup as markdown.
cat("```{=html}", readLines("assets/schedule-builder.html"), "```", sep = "\n")
```

### What to do with the file {-}

Save it as `schedule.json` and put it on the device's SD card, inside the folder named after the device, replacing the one there: `<DEVICE_ID>/schedule.json` ([Settings on the SD card](device.html#sd-files)). If the device is already on the network, you can skip the card and use **Upload Schedule** in the Commander's Actions tab instead. To run the same experiment on several devices, put the same file in each device's folder.

Uploading a schedule does not interrupt a run already in progress --- reset the scheduler from the Actions tab to pick up the new file.

One thing the form deliberately allows, because it is sometimes what you want: **setpoints that fall outside the cycle length.** These are flagged, not blocked, since you may be mid-edit --- but a setpoint after the end of the cycle is never reached.
